data.long_meaning: One who has good conduct, who is virtuous, and who is auspicious. A name of Vishnu. The name Shusil carries the meaning “Good, virtuous, auspicious” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Hindu tradition and is also used in Sanskrit, Hindi. Parents who choose Shusil usually hope their child will grow to embody good, virtuous, auspicious and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.etymology: Shusil belongs to the Hindu linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Good, virtuous, auspicious.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Shusil total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

data.cultural_impact: The name "Shusil" has been in use for centuries among Hindus, particularly in India. It is a Sanskrit name, and its meaning, "one who has good conduct, who is virtuous, and who is auspicious," continues to resonate within the Indian cultural fabric. A person named Shusil is often perceived as an embodiment of moral excellence, values that are highly cherished and celebrated in Hindu society. The name evokes images of virtuous leaders and sages, thus inspiring individuals to strive for moral integrity and righteousness in their own lives.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name "Shusil" also holds deep significance. It is derived from the Sanskrit words "shu" (good) and "sila" (conduct). As a name of Vishnu, Shusil represents the god's divine qualities of morality, righteousness, and virtue. It is a reminder that a true spiritual path must be built on these foundations. For the bearer of the name, it carries the blessings of Lord Vishnu, inspiring one to lead a virtuous and auspicious life. By embodying the virtues of this name, a person is believed to come closer to attaining spiritual growth and enlightenment.
data.spiritual_symbolism: The name Shusil symbolizes purity, virtue, and moral uprightness. It is derived from the Sanskrit word 'shushila' which means 'pure', reflecting an individual's inner goodness and moral character.

historical_references.reference: Shusil was a renowned poet, philosopher, and teacher in ancient India. He is believed to have lived during the late Gupta period (5th to 6th century AD).
historical_references.time_period: Late Gupta period (5th to 6th century AD)

historical_references.reference: Shusil is also known as Shankara Bhagavatpada or Shankaracharya. He is considered as the founder of the Advaita Vedanta philosophy, which emphasizes the non-dualistic concept of Brahman.

modern_usage.modern_context: The name 'Shusil' is of Hindu origin and translates to 'pure' or 'sincere'. In the modern context, it is often used as a name for individuals who are deeply committed to spirituality, personal growth, and self-improvement. On LinkedIn, you might find a professional named Shusil who lists 'mindfulness' or 'meditation' as a skill. On YouTube, there could be a channel named 'Shusil Speaks' focused on delivering enlightening and insightful talks on spirituality and personal development.
